title: A Satellite Dish Through the Shingles
description: Lag bolts through a shingle are a leak on the next hard Houston rain. Mount the dish on the wall or a flashed bracket, and close the old holes.
html:
The dish can be dead and the holes can still be working. Installers lagged brackets through the shingles, dabbed sealant on the heads, and left. The sealant cracked. The lags loosened. Rain follows the threads into the deck. We find this on roofs that “never leaked until this year,” under a dish nobody has aimed since the house changed TV plans.

Where a dish should sit

The clean mount is not on the shingle field. A gable wall, the fascia, or a bracket that is flashed like any other penetration gives the cable a place to land without a raw hole in the roof. If the only clear shot to the satellite is the roof, the mount still needs metal that laps into the courses, not four bolts and a tube of tar. The same rule fits dish replacements, weather stations, and the unused cable entry somebody stuffed with foam.

Abandoned hardware should come off. Filling the holes with caulk and leaving the bracket is how the leak stays. We pull the lags, patch the deck if the wood is soft, and weave new shingles or a flashed plate so the repair is a roof detail. Matching the shingles may not be perfect. Watertight matters more than a dish you no longer use.

Do not add another hole to diagnose it

From the attic, the stain is often a small dark circle at the lag, easy to confuse with a pipe boot a few feet away. Look at both before anyone cuts. If you are about to have a new service installed, tell them the roof is not the default. If the old one is already dripping, that is a roof repair with the dish coming down as part of it.

Call (281) 541-0027 or request a free inspection. Point us at the dish, even if you think the TV is the only thing that quit.
